en: Those devotees who, always united, worship you in this way, and those who worship the imperishable, the unmanifest: which of them know yoga better?
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।
tr: mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate
en: Those who fix their minds on me and worship me, always united, with supreme faith: I consider them the most perfect in yoga.
speaker: Krishna said

en: But those who worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest, all-pervading and unthinkable, unchanging, immovable and eternal,
restraining all the senses, even-minded everywhere, delighting in the good of all beings: they too come to me.
The difficulty is greater for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest, for the path of the unmanifest is hard for embodied beings to reach.

sa: ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः।
tr: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ
en: But those who offer all actions to me, intent on me, and worship me, meditating on me with undivided yoga,
for them, whose minds have entered into me, I soon become the one who lifts them out of the ocean of death and rebirth, Partha.

sa: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय।
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
tr: mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya
nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
en: Fix your mind on me alone; let your understanding rest in me. Then, without doubt, you will live in me from now on.

sa: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम्।
tr: atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram
en: If you cannot keep your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of practice, Dhananjaya.
If you cannot even practise, be devoted to working for me; doing actions for my sake, you will still reach perfection.
If you cannot do even this, then, taking refuge in my yoga and controlling yourself, give up the fruits of all your actions.
Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruits of action is better than meditation, for peace follows renunciation at once.

sa: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।
tr: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca
en: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from "mine" and from ego, even in pain and pleasure, and forgiving,
always content, a yogi, self-controlled, firm in resolve, with mind and understanding offered to me: such a devotee is dear to me.

sa: हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः ॥
tr: harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ
en: One by whom the world is not disturbed and who is not disturbed by the world, who is free from elation, impatience, fear and anxiety, is dear to me.

sa: सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः ॥
tr: sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ
en: One who expects nothing, is pure, capable, impartial and untroubled, who has given up every self-centred undertaking: such a devotee is dear to me.

sa: यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।
tr: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati
en: One who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor craves, who has let go of good and bad, and is full of devotion, is dear to me.

sa: समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः।
tr: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
en: Alike to enemy and friend, alike in honour and dishonour, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, free from attachment,
the same in blame and praise, quiet, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion: that person is dear to me.
But those who follow this nectar of dharma as I have taught it, with faith, making me their goal: those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.
